content.text:
I submitted **index 10 (Bi 0.436, V 0.564)** as the best composition. At 2.33e-5 A it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, which used the whole merit budget.

| Index | Bi : V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.49 : 0.51 | 5.3e-6 |
| **10** | **0.44 : 0.56** | **2.33e-5** |
| 4 | 0.43 : 0.57 | 1.41e-5 |

- **Why I started near BiVO₄:** it's the known strong photoanode in this system, and the model checks supported it. One model puts it essentially on the stability limit (0.008 eV/atom above the convex hull). Another predicts a band gap of about 2.99 eV, low enough to absorb the 3.22 eV illumination.
- **What the results show:** the exact 1:1 composition was weak. Adding a little extra vanadium raised the photocurrent about 4×, and going further dropped it again, so the peak is near V ≈ 0.56.
- **Main gap:** I never measured any Bi-rich composition (Bi ≥ 0.56). I skipped that side because the V-rich trend looked more promising and Bi-rich films tend to form phases that are weaker photoanodes. That's a judgement, not a measurement, so a better Bi-rich composition can't be ruled out.
- **XRD not used:** none of the 5 XRD measurements were spent, so the phases in the films weren't checked directly.
